anya: Heads up — seeing sustained memory growth on prod for Mistral-7B-MQA when sessions hit ~80k tokens and we reuse KV heavily. Not classic leak — looks like paging + fragmentation. @kevin can you take a look?

kevin: Which node/model exactly? any profiler output? :thinking:

anya: repro on node-14, model=mistral-7b-mqa-2025. Quick profiler snippet:
```
kv_pages_allocated:  512 -> 2048 (over ~30s)
kv_live_slots:       480 -> 1536
fragmentation_ratio: 0.67
page_faults/sec:     18
context_tokens:      82000
heap_peak_mb:         12480
heap_current_mb:      12240
```
Repro steps: start a long-chat stream that appends ~2k tokens every 2s, interleave short chat requests (<=64 tokens) from other clients to trigger shard mixing.

runtime-bot: ALERT node-14: OOM kill (container r-inference-42) at 2025-11-18T12:34:12Z

olga: This smells like MQA grouping + rope scaling mismatch. MQA stores grouped heads per-kv page size; when rope scaling changes effective seq_len, we end up allocating extra small pages and cannot reuse them across requests -> fragmentation. We saw similar with qwen-gqa but more pronounced here.

mike: Also note batching heuristics: when small requests interleave with the long session, the runtime mixes batches and copies KV ranges across buffers to satisfy latency SLOs, which creates duplicate pages and pressure. We should try affinity-based batching (sticky to same worker) to improve KV reuse.

kevin: Good calls. Two hypotheses: (1) allocator fragmentation due to variable page sizes + group heads, (2) fused matmul kernel temporarily allocates scratch for MQA path which triggers eviction. Try toggling kernel selection: `--kernels=fallback` or `--no-fused-matmul` to see if peak drops.

anya: Ran quick test with kernel toggle: peak heap dropped ~9% but fragmentation still high. Patch idea: switch to slab allocator for KV pages with fixed-size buckets aligned to grouped-head sizes, plus an LRU per-model-variant so pages can be reused across sessions.

olga: Agreed. Also add a normalize_rope_stride() pass when loading MQA variants so cached KV lengths map to a canonical bucket where possible. That will reduce equivalent-but-offset caches.

mike: For batching, short-term: change heuristics to prefer worker-affinity for requests that reference an active context id. Pseudocode:
```
if request.context_id in active_contexts: route_to(context_owner)
else: route_to(short_latency_pool)
```
This prevented most of the cross-copy hits in my local sim.

kevin: Ops note: schedule a small A/B on node-14: branch `kv-slab-mqa` vs `main` with kernel flag off for the branch. Measure `fragmentation_ratio` and `kv_pages_allocated` over 1h windows. If slab reduces fragmentation by >30% and pages_allocated by >25% we roll to prod.

anya: I'll prepare the repro harness and metrics dashboard. Putting initial numbers into the ticket. Can someone volunteer to run the A/B tomorrow morning (UTC)? :raised_hand:

olga: volunteering. PR coming in a few hrs: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR-xxxx (WIP)

mike: I'll add the routing change to the heuristics repo and a tiny integration test.

kevin: I'll validate kernel interplay and run kernel-bench to see transient scratch allocations.

anya: Thanks all. Adding a short checklist in the ticket:
- run A/B (olga)
- run kernel-bench + profile (kevin)
- add affinity heuristic & test (mike)
- repro harness + dashboard (anya)

kevin: also capture a heap snapshot at ~90k tokens for both branches. saves diagnosing later. :thumbsup:

olga: noted. tagging runtime-sre for monitoring dashboards.

anya: Great — will update thread with results.
